implementationPlan.description: GUARD + BASELINE. (a) Confirm packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/__fixtures__/toolsHarness.ts exists. If it does NOT, slice 1 (task-4f541baba99b458da14bf8250d88af4c) has not landed — call moe.report_blocked immediately and do not build a second harness; two harnesses is the one outcome that makes slices 3 and 4 unmergeable. (b) Read the harness fully: note that testDir/moePath/state are GETTERS (never destructure them — state is reassigned each beforeEach, so a copy goes stale and later tests silently run against a dead StateManager) while setupMoeFolder/createEpic/createTask/createWorker are stable functions safe to destructure. (c) From packages/moe-daemon run `npx vitest run 2>&1 | tail -30`, record the `Tests   N passed` total and any failing files as this slice's baseline — the fleet shares one uncommitted tree so pre-existing red may belong to another task (mem:gotcha-shared-tree-red-suite); never stash or revert it. (d) Confirm `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. (e) In tools.test.ts, locate this slice's 9 blocks BY NAME (the task description's line numbers are stale — slice 1 removed 8 describes ahead of them) and record each one's `it` count. Expected: list_tasks 5, get_next_task 4, create_task 3, create_epic 2, set_task_status 4, delete_task 3, update_epic 5, delete_epic 4, search_tasks 6 — 36 total. If a count differs, an earlier slice touched a block it did not own; stop and report_blocked rather than guessing.

implementationPlan.description: MOVE THE TASK-SIDE READ/CREATE BLOCKS. Permitted edits only: the import header, `const h = useToolsHarness();`, a destructure of the stable helpers, and h.-prefixed mutable references (h.state / h.testDir / h.moePath). Each file imports only the tool factory it exercises (listTasksTool / getNextTaskTool / createTaskTool) plus the schema types its assertions actually name — do not copy tools.test.ts's whole import block into each file. Watch the identifier collision: the harness helper `createTask` and the imported `createTaskTool` coexist in createTask.test.ts; if you destructure `createTask` there, confirm nothing shadows the import. Delete each block from tools.test.ts as you go. Run `npx vitest run src/tools/listTasks.test.ts src/tools/getNextTask.test.ts src/tools/createTask.test.ts` and assert 12 tests pass — exactly the 5+4+3 recorded in step 1.
implementationPlan.note: Verified already-landed a22af4c move: listTasks/getNextTask/createTask contain exactly 5+4+3=12 tests and use the single ToolTestHarness. Focused Vitest passed 3 files / 12 tests. All expect lines are byte-identical to the parent block after only permitted h.state/h.testDir/h.moePath fixture normalization. No new edits were needed.

implementationPlan.description: MOVE THE EPIC-SIDE BLOCKS. Create createEpic.test.ts, updateEpic.test.ts and deleteEpic.test.ts. Note the concurrent StateManager split (task-1bc9d7a899724caa87d1df962658e1f6) is moving validateEpicUpdates into src/state/validators.ts in the same working tree — it stays behavior-identical, so these tests must keep passing unchanged; if they fail with a state/* error, that is the other task mid-edit, not yours. implementationPlan.note: Verified pre-landed createEpic/updateEpic/deleteEpic move: focused Vitest passed 3 files / 11 tests (2+5+4). Every expect line matches the parent tools.test.ts block after fixture-reference normalization, preserving specific validator error assertions. No new edits needed.

implementationPlan.description: MOVE THE STATUS/DELETE BLOCKS. Create setTaskStatus.test.ts and deleteTask.test.ts. The set_task_status block covers the human-gated transitions (BACKLOG -> PLANNING/WORKING/REVIEW are all legal; agent-claimable columns are not the same set) and may overlap coverage in lifecycleFixes.test.ts — do NOT merge, dedupe or drop anything that looks redundant. implementationPlan.note: Verified pre-landed setTaskStatus/deleteTask move: focused Vitest passed 2 files / 7 tests (4+3), and all expect lines match the parent blocks after fixture-reference normalization. No overlapping coverage was deduplicated. No new edits needed.

implementationPlan.description: APPEND search_tasks — the only APPEND in this slice and the one real hazard. searchTasks.test.ts ALREADY defines its own top-level `function setupMoeFolder(testDir: string): string`, a different signature from the harness's `setupMoeFolder(projectOverrides?: Partial<Project>)`. In this file destructure NOTHING from the harness: append `describe('moe.search_tasks')` (6 its) as a TOP-LEVEL describe with its own `const h = useToolsHarness();` and call every helper explicitly — h.setupMoeFolder(...), h.createTask(...), h.state — so the moved block never touches the file's local fixture and the local fixture never touches the harness. Do not nest the moved block inside the file's existing describe, and do not refactor the existing tests onto the harness; that is scope this task does not own. Confirm the two fixtures allocate INDEPENDENT temp dirs — the file's own setupMoeFolder takes a testDir argument while the harness mkdtemps its own, so they should not overlap, but verify rather than assume: run `npx vitest run src/tools/searchTasks.test.ts` ALONE and then again as part of the full directory, and assert the same count both ways. A shared temp dir makes test order matter and shows up as a flake days later. Delete the block from tools.test.ts. Assert searchTasks.test.ts now reports its original count + 6.
implementationPlan.note: Verified pre-landed search_tasks append. searchTasks.test.ts has exactly two top-level describes, one original local setupMoeFolder definition, and the moved block uses its own ToolTestHarness instance with explicit h.setupMoeFolder/h.createTask/h.state access. Isolated run passed 10/10 (original 4 + moved 6); the earlier full-suite run also passed all 866. Moved expect lines are identical after fixture normalization. No new edits needed.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Grouping the eight new files by subject (task-side, epic-side, status/delete) rather than one step per file: keeps the plan at 7 steps instead of 12 while each step stays a single reviewable concern, and every one of these blocks is small (2-5 `it`s). searchTasks gets its own step because it is the only APPEND in this slice and carries the fixture-collision hazard — mixing it into a batch step is how that collision gets missed.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured BEFORE slice 1 runs, so treat every line number as stale and address blocks by describe NAME. What does not go stale is the per-block `it` count — use it as the move contract: list_tasks 5, get_next_task 4, create_task 3, create_epic 2, set_task_status 4, delete_task 3, update_epic 5, delete_epic 4, search_tasks 6. **Total 36 `it`s across this slice's 9 blocks, ~465 lines.** The harness from slice 1 (src/tools/__fixtures__/toolsHarness.ts) exposes testDir/moePath/state as GETTERS plus four stable destructurable helpers (setupMoeFolder, createEpic, createTask, createWorker) — see mem:daemon/tools-test-split-slices for the full design and why the getter shape is mandatory. claimNextTask.test.ts is the reference for how a colocated tool test should look.
planningNotes.risks:
FIXTURE COLLISION — the one real hazard in this slice: searchTasks.test.ts already defines its OWN top-level `function setupMoeFolder(testDir: string): string`, a DIFFERENT signature from the harness's `setupMoeFolder(projectOverrides?: Partial<Project>)`. Destructuring the harness helper into that file shadows or clashes with the local one and the failure is a confusing type error at best, a silently-wrong temp project at worst. In that file use `h.setupMoeFolder(...)` explicitly and destructure NOTHING.
STALE LINE NUMBERS: slice 1 removes 8 describes from tools.test.ts before this task runs. Locate blocks by `describe('moe.list_tasks'` etc., never by the line numbers in the task description.
STALE-BINDING TRAP (inherited): never `const { state } = h` — state is reassigned every beforeEach, so a destructured copy goes stale after the first test and later tests silently run against a dead StateManager. Only the four helper functions are safe to destructure.
DEPENDENCY: if src/tools/__fixtures__/toolsHarness.ts does not exist, slice 1 has not landed — moe.report_blocked, do NOT build a second harness. Two harnesses is the one outcome that makes slices 3 and 4 unmergeable.
SHARED DIRTY TREE: the fleet works in one uncommitted tree and `npm test` can be red from other tasks (mem:gotcha-shared-tree-red-suite). Baseline first; 'green' means no NEW failing file. Never stash or revert another task's work.
NO DEDUPING: createTask.test.ts / createEpic.test.ts are new files, but setTaskStatus and deleteEpic coverage may overlap lifecycleFixes.test.ts. Do not merge or drop a test that looks redundant — identical test count is the cross-slice DoD and slice 4 checks the final number against slice 1's recorded baseline.
